claim: Standard fixed-length sequence concatenation with causal masking lets each token attend to tokens from previous, unrelated documents, injecting distracting context that measurably degrades language-modelling and downstream performance.
stance_target: The repo's data-pipeline assumption that naive packing with causal masking is a neutral implementation detail
scope_conditions: 1.3B-parameter LLaMA-architecture models, 150B SlimPajama tokens, 2K and 8K context
quoted_support: we find that applying causal masking can lead to the inclusion of distracting information from previous documents during pre-training, which negatively impacts the performance of the models on language modelling and downstream tasks.

claim: Intra-document causal masking, where each token is conditioned only on preceding tokens of the same document, significantly improves performance over causal masking across LM and downstream tasks.
stance_target: The repo's option of document-boundary-aware attention masking as a data-pipeline design choice
scope_conditions: INTRADoc variant, 1.3B models, 2K and 8K context, SlimPajama
quoted_support: In intra-document causal masking, the likelihood of each token is only conditioned on the previous tokens in the same document, eliminating potential distracting information from previous documents and significantly improving performance.

claim: The retrieval-based packing method BM25Chunk improves in-context learning by 11.6%, knowledge memorisation by 9.8% and context utilisation by 7.2% without sacrificing training efficiency.
stance_target: That packing strategy is a first-order quality lever available to a small-scale run at no throughput cost
scope_conditions: BM25Chunk sequence construction, 1.3B models, 2K and 8K context
quoted_support: our proposed efficient retrieval-based sequence construction method, Bm25Chunk, can improve in-context learning (+11.6%), knowledge memorisation (+9.8%), and context utilisation (+7.2%) abilities of language models without sacrificing efficiency.
